title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: CrowdStrike Falcon
providers.scope_notes: Public developer docs only; Falcon console documentation (IP allowlisting, audit event names, roles) requires login and is marked unknown. Next-Gen SIEM HEC needs a Next-Gen SIEM subscription; member_cid needs Flight Control.

controls.name: Regenerate Ingest token
controls.what: Regenerates the data connection ingest token.

controls_unknown: IP allowlisting for API clients: whether it exists, whether it applies to /oauth2/token or every API request (Falcon docs require login).
Whether deleting an API client or resetting its secret invalidates already-issued 30-minute tokens.
Audit event names for API client create/update/delete/secret reset and token issuance, and which field carries the client ID.
Whether ordinary API read calls are written to the audit log, and audit log retention.
Which Falcon roles can create API clients, and whether creation can require approval.
Whether a parent CID can be prevented from issuing member_cid tokens for specific child CIDs.
HEC ingest key expiry, IP restriction, and whether regeneration invalidates the old key immediately.
API rate limits (documented only inside Falcon).

auth_paths.name: Next-Gen SIEM HEC data connector API key (ingest token)

authentication.summary: Creating an HEC/HTTP Event Data Connector produces an API key and URL used by log shippers to send events into Next-Gen SIEM.

lifetime.summary: Token has an expires_at timestamp; default and max not documented

administration.summary: Next-Gen SIEM > Data ingestion > Data connectors.
administration.conditions: Falcon Next-Gen SIEM subscription; Administrator or Connector Manager.

offboard.details: The key belongs to the data connector, shown on the connector's detail page.

inventory.details: GET /ngsiem/combined/connections/v1 lists data connections; console page Next-Gen SIEM > Data ingestion > Data connectors.

usage.ui: Next-Gen SIEM > Data ingestion > Data connectors > <connector> > Show events (or Advanced Event Search filtered on the connector's #connector tag)

log_sources.name: Next-Gen SIEM events tagged #connector
log_sources.notes: Ingested data can be filtered by the connector tag; key-use audit not documented.

anomaly_cues: Unexpected events or volume on a connector (log injection)

containment.steps: Regenerate the ingest token or delete the connector.
containment.notes: Regenerating the ingest token invalidates the previous one; timing not stated.

unknown: Audit events for connector key regeneration
Ingest key is write-only per docs reviewed; read capability not documented
